note: Observed spike_count=13.5 after hyperpolarising conditioning matches H1 prediction [12,18]. Data confirms slow-deactivating inward current hypothesis.

text: H2 (slow Na recovery) predicted spike_count ∈ [0,8] after hyperpolarising conditioning, but P3 probe measured 13.5. The gap of 5.5 spikes (with reps=2 averaged) cannot be explained by variance. H2's core mechanism - that slow Na channel recovery reduces firing - contradicts the data. The observed 13.5 spikes aligns with H1's prediction [12,18] of a slow-deactivating inward current. H2 is refuted by this probe.

H3 claims both slow-deactivating inward current AND slow Na recovery contribute. P3 probe refuted H2's slow Na recovery component (predicted [0,8], observed 13.5). Since one of H3's two proposed mechanisms is incorrect, H3's combined model is not supported. H1 alone explains the data without requiring the additional slow Na component.

note: P8 probe measured 13.5 spikes, which is outside H2's predicted band [0,8]. The observation falls in the kill band [13,15] for H2. H2 (slow Na recovery) is refuted.

P8 probe measured 13.5 spikes, which falls in H3's support band [12, 18]. However, H3 claims a combined mechanism including both slow-deactivating inward current AND slow Na recovery. Since H2 (slow Na recovery) was just refuted by the same probe (13.5 outside H2's [0,8] band), H3's combined mechanism is incorrect. H3 is refuted because it includes a wrong component.

text: H1 SUPPORTED by P3/P8 probes (13.5 spikes in [12,18]), but the hypothesis ignores several constraints: (1) The 'slow-deactivating inward current' is not identified — could be HCN, persistent Na, or T-type Ca2+; the campaign only characterized kinetics, not molecular identity. (2) The forecast for held-out protocols assumed linear voltage-dependence of deactivation, but real currents may have non-monotonic I-V relationships. (3) Campaign only tested seed 0 of ca_rebound world; kinetics may vary across seeds. (4) No voltage-clamp data to directly measure the current's reversal potential or conductance. (5) The 40-spike response after depolarizing conditioning may saturate — H1 predicts enhancement but not ceiling effects. These are scope constraints, not refutations.
